gap: No result ChatGPT got states, as a pairing rule, that the ANTHBOT N8 can only collect with its Cyclone blade disc plus grass bag fitted, that mulching needs a different disc that is screwed on underneath plus a deflector, and that the 4G NetRTK link is free for the first year only and then costs $35.99 a year.
standout_why: I compared against the cited PCWorld, T3, Notebookcheck YUKA and mammotion.com/pages/yuka pages, plus the uncited neointell, mowerbotlab and Notebookcheck N8 pages. PCWorld (cited) already has the Cyclone/Particle disc swap and the $35.99-a-year 4G fee. T3 (cited) already says mulching needs a different disc and a chute in place of the bag. Notebookcheck's YUKA review (cited) already has the sweeper cutting the slope limit from 45% to 18% (10°). ChatGPT's answers did not pass on the disc swap or the 4G fee, but the cited rivals contain them. Neither neointell nor mowerbotlab names any compatible accessory pairing.
decides: It confirms the N8 as the pick. Bagging is its default factory setup: it ships with the collecting disc fitted and includes an RTK reference station, so it works without the paid 4G service. On the YUKA side, the maker's spec sheet lists the sweeper slope limit only for the full-size YUKA 1500/2000, and the maker's YUKA page attaches the sweeper kit only to full-size YUKA. Shoppers should not expect the cheaper YUKA mini or mini 2 to bag.

findings.label: Collect vs mulch configuration
findings.value: Collecting uses the Cyclone blade disc with the grass catcher. Mulching uses the Particle disc. The two blade types are not interchangeable, and changing discs means loosening screws underneath. The app greys out mulching while the catcher is fitted.
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: From PCWorld's hands-on review, tested on firmware 0.3.90.

findings.label: Factory configuration
findings.value: Ships with the grass-collecting disc fitted. Mulching means changing to the six-blade disc and replacing the rear collection bag with the mulching chute.
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 robot lawn mower review | T3

findings.label: Attachment requirement and box contents
findings.value: Will not run unless either the basket or the discharge deflector is fitted. The box holds the collection bag, deflector, charging station, RTK reference station with a mast just over 1.5 m tall, screwdriver, mulching disc (6 blades) and 3 spare blades. No garage is included.
findings.source_title: This robotic lawn mower makes sense in autumn too: Anthbot N8 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck's review. This result was in ChatGPT's list but was not cited.

findings.label: 4G / NetRTK service cost
findings.value: Free for the first year, then $35.99 for 1 year, $75.99 for 2 years or $107.99 for 3 years. Without the RTK antenna the mower uses NetRTK over mobile networks. Wi-Fi is 2.4 and 5 GHz, and setup pairs over Bluetooth.
findings.note: T3's spec box says '4G data: One year included'. Since the RTK station comes in the box, the subscription is optional.

findings.label: Dump-area rules
findings.value: Up to 5 dump areas, each at least 5 × 5 ft, inside the mowing zone (PCWorld). Notebookcheck says 1 to 5 areas, which cannot be too close to the lawn edge and may lie outside the mapped area.
findings.note: The two reviews disagree on whether a dump area may sit outside the map. The maker's manual would settle it, but I could not open it (see unsourced).

findings.label: Area per run with catcher fitted
findings.value: About 2,150 sq ft of continuous mowing with the catcher fitted (Anthbot's claim, as reported by PCWorld). In PCWorld's test, 1,200 sq ft took 97 minutes and 960 sq ft used about 80% of the battery. Recharging takes 80 minutes.
findings.note: This is per charge, not the 1,500 m² (0.37 acre) total-area rating.

findings.label: Fixed emptying interval
findings.value: Empties automatically every 100 minutes. Notebookcheck found no setting to change the interval.
findings.note: PCWorld instead says the robot detects when the box is full.

findings.label: Maker's model listing and manual
findings.value: Listed as '1500㎡ | Mow, Mulch, Collect, Sweep | 4G'. The manual is the 'N-RTK User Manual', filed under 'N8 RTK'. N-series accessories are a Power Adapter for Charging Station ($49), an RTK Wall Mount Kit ($79) and an RTK Extension Cable ($49).
findings.note: The visible applicability text for the two RTK accessories names Genie, M5 and M9 and was cut off before any N8 mention.

findings.label: Slope limit with vs without Sweeper Kit (maker spec)
findings.value: 28° without the sweeper; 18% (10°) with the sweeper. Max area is 1,500 m² (0.37 acre) for the YUKA 1500 and 2,000 m² (0.5 acre) for the YUKA 2000. Cutting height is 30–100 mm in the US and 20–90 mm in EU/AU/UK.
findings.note: The maker's spec sheet covers only the YUKA 1500 and 2000. It does not cover the 1000, 3000 or mini models.

findings.label: Sweeper kit on maker's YUKA line page
findings.value: The 'easy-to-attach sweeper kit' / '2-in-1 Self-empty Lawn Sweeper Kit' is attached only to YUKA (1,000–3,000 m²). The YUKA mini (600–800 m²), YUKA mini 2 800 and YUKA mini 2 1000 entries carry no sweeper mention. The iNavi service is 'currently accessible in Germany'.
findings.source_title: Mammotion YUKA: Self-Emptying Sweeper Robot Lawn Mower
findings.note: The page leaves the mini models out of the sweeper claim but does not explicitly exclude them. The footnote on the sweeper claim was not shown.

findings.label: Sweeper add-on and bundles
findings.value: The sweeper is optional and costs 699 euros (~US$799) on its own. The Yuka 1000 and 2000 are also sold as bundles with it. The slope limit drops from 45% (24°) to 18% (10°) with the sweeper, and it ran at almost 70 dB. The iNavi NetRTK service was free until the end of 2025, with 2026 pricing unannounced.
findings.note: Notebookcheck tested the Yuka 1000 (EU). Its 45% no-sweeper figure differs from the 28° on the maker's 1500/2000 spec sheet.

unsourced: The Sweeper Kit's own US product page (us.mammotion.com/products/sweeper-kit-for-yuka-series) for its compatible-model list, today's price and stock: every Mammotion store domain (us, ca, eu, uk, au, mammotion.com) returned HTTP 429 or 403, and storecheck.py also returned HTTP 403.

A maker statement on whether the Sweeper Kit fits the YUKA 1000 and 3000 or explicitly excludes the YUKA mini and mini 2: the support installation article showed only its title, and the manuals.plus copy of the kit manual returned 403.

The ANTHBOT N-RTK User Manual PDF (cdn.shopify.com/.../N_-RTK-_-EN-20260320.pdf), for the maker's own wording on disc swaps, dump-area rules and slope with the catcher fitted: the file is over 10 MB, too large for the page reader, and downloading it was not permitted in this session.
The slope rating with the N8's catcher fitted: the 45% (24°) rating does not say whether the catcher is attached.
